report.source_text: The tumor was surgically removed via a transconjunctival approach along inferior rectus muscle. Intraoperatively, the tumor was completely separated from muscle tissue since it was pseudoencapsular. The gross specimen exhibited a firm fibrotic nodule-like and pale-colored mass (Fig. 3). There was no significant improvement in globe mobility after surgery; however, a longer term follow-up is required.

clinician.final_diagnosis: granular cell tumor (GCT) of the inferior rectus muscle
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 45-year-old man presented with a 3-year history of vertical diplopia and marked visual acuity decrease when gazing upward. Orbital MRI identified a nodule-like tumor in the inferior rectus muscle with characteristic T1 and T2 signal intensities. Subsequent biopsy and histopathological examination revealed an encapsulated tumor with large nested cells, positive immunostaining for CD68, S100, and vimentin, and negative for CK, consistent with granular cell tumor. The tumor was surgically resected via a transconjunctival approach, with no immediate improvement in globe mobility but requiring long-term follow-up.
